title: Understanding Orthogonality
text: Orthogonality in linear algebra refers to vectors being perpendicular to each other. If two vectors are orthogonal, their dot product is zero.

title: Vector of Ones
text: The vector \( \mathbf{1} \) is a special vector where all elements are $$1$$. It is often used in linear algebra to represent constant terms or to check orthogonality with other vectors.

title: Residuals in OLS
text: In an OLS model, the residuals are the differences between the true outcomes \( Y \) and the predicted outcomes \( \hat{Y} \).

title: Checking Orthogonality
text: To determine if \( \mathbf{1} \) is orthogonal to \( Y-\hat{Y} \), consider the dot product of \( \mathbf{1} \) and \( Y-\hat{Y} \). If the dot product is zero, they are orthogonal.
